searchText: It'd be great if no one else runs miners on Kiln. If you know anyone running a miner, please ask them to stop it 🙂 Its crazy hard to estimate when TTD happens on these testnets since we have no idea what hashpower will join in. It's a biiit easier to do if we control all the miners. <@&836981603216654336> is that you perhaps? saw a bunch of mining-related PRs open this AM 🙂 There was a batch of blocks last night that we mined with stratum but it was for just like 60 seconds. <@!199561711278227457> would you post that ask on twitter and I will socialize it? sure 🙂 we have 3 cpu miners that are active, but they are suuuuper low hashrate Oh yeah seeing a bunch of reorgs atm Yea, i'd say its a gpu miner not us that said, when we get closer to TTD besu would like to gpu mine so we can test that our stratum miner correctly stops there I followed this guide: https://notes.ethereum.org/qrDBhhydTsyKFmGaBl2COQ on how to run a node on Kiln. I tried with Lighthouse, Prysm and Lodestar and couldn't have a single one to run. That's because the author just copy-pasted instruction out of context. When you execute the commands one after the other as prompted by the guide, you can't get a single consensus layer to run. There are inconsistencies between the actual state of my machine when I follow the guide and the command I'm prompted to execute. That make it impossible to run a Kiln node by following this guide. Which is sad, because it is the only purpose of this guide. Some interesting guides for doing your Kiln setup: - Geth+Lighthouse: https://github.com/remyroy/ethstaker/blob/main/merge-devnet.md - Geth+Teku: https://agstakingco.gitbook.io/kiln-testnet-ethereum-staking-guide/ I added some basic instruction for prysm and geth here: https://hackmd.io/@prysmaticlabs/B1Q2SluWq

excerpts.author: parithosh
excerpts.content:
It'd be great if no one else runs miners on Kiln. If you know anyone running a miner, please ask them to stop it 🙂

Its crazy hard to estimate when TTD happens on these testnets since we have no idea what hashpower will join in. It's a biiit easier to do if we control all the miners.

excerpts.author: tdelabro
excerpts.content:
I followed this guide: https://notes.ethereum.org/qrDBhhydTsyKFmGaBl2COQ on how to run a node on Kiln.
I tried with Lighthouse, Prysm and Lodestar and couldn't have a single one to run. That's because the author just copy-pasted instruction out of context. When you execute the commands one after the other as prompted by the guide, you can't get a single consensus layer to run. There are inconsistencies between the actual state of my machine when I follow the guide and the command I'm prompted to execute. That make it impossible to run a Kiln node by following this guide. Which is sad, because it is the only purpose of this guide.
